chunks: From him, from some of the Kufans, he traces it back to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Regarding a man who has intercourse with his wife from behind while she is fasting, he said: 'It does not break her fast, and there is no ghusl (ritual bath) upon her.'

key_terms.دُبُر: The rear/anus, referring to the site of intercourse

ai.seo_question: Does sexual intercourse from behind break a woman's fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that sexual intercourse from behind does not break the fast of the woman, nor does it obligate her to perform ghusl, distinguishing it from other forms of intercourse. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it highlights the specific conditions under which sexual acts invalidate fasting, emphasizing that the act itself does not nullify the fast unless accompanied by ejaculation or other specific factors. The hadith is found in Tahdhib al-Ahkam, a key hadith collection by Shaykh al-Tusi, and reflects the detailed legal discussions on marital relations during Ramadan.
